_ruling: RULING B, 2026-09-25. The drafted tiers were INVERTED and are corrected here. additional-extension-form-4868 is the only terminal that asks the reader to file an instrument (Form 4868) before a date, so it carries the live obligation: 147/amber/critical. overseas-auto-extension and military-overseas-extension describe an extension granted AUTOMATICALLY with nothing to lodge - the interest-accrual sentence the drafter matched on is a note, not money conditionally at stake - so both are 67/green/standard. Escape heading/result_copy remain the hand-authored versions from ruling A.

none_fit.heading: This check covers US expat filing — yours may sit outside it
none_fit.result_copy: This check answers four things for US citizens and resident aliens living abroad: the filing extensions you get automatically and how to extend further, whether the Foreign Earned Income Exclusion or the Foreign Tax Credit fits your income, when foreign accounts trigger FBAR or FATCA reporting, and whether a US state still has a claim on you. Your answers do not place you in any of those. That is not a verdict that nothing applies to you — it means this check is the wrong instrument for the question you are asking. If you are a US person abroad with an unresolved filing question, a short personalised review establishes which rules actually govern it.

insufficient_information.heading: Your answers do not settle your filing position yet
insufficient_information.result_copy: One detail needed to reach a conclusion is still unconfirmed — most often whether you were physically abroad on the regular due date, whether your foreign accounts crossed a reporting threshold, or whether you severed ties with your last US state. Each of those changes the answer, so naming a position now would mean guessing, and on a US filing obligation a guess is worse than no answer. A short personalised review works through the missing detail and sets out where you actually stand on extensions, FEIE or FTC, FBAR and FATCA, and state tax.
